newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-INJURIES DELAY SPRINGBOK TEAM SELECTION.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-INJURIES DELAY SPRINGBOK TEAM SELECTION.

text.p: Springbok centre Edrich Lubbe will miss the rest of the series against the British Lions as South African face a number of injury worries, team officials said on Monday.
Coach Carel du Plessis has had to delay naming his side for Saturday's second test in Durban until Wednesday because of doubts over several players.

"There are just so many injury worries -- both major and minor -- in the squad that we have had to delay the announcement until Wednesday morning," media liaison officer Herman Coetzee told Reuters on Monday.
Lubbe has been ruled out for between two to four weeks with a pulled hamstring while there was still concern over his midfield partner Japie Mulder who has a shoulder injury.

"Edrich will probably only be able to play again in time for the Tri-Nations series with New Zealand and Australia and Japie is seeing a specialist in Johannesburg today about his damaged left shoulder," Coetzee said.
"Japie says his shoulder is sore but he can't really determine how serious the injury is. He flew up to see the Johannesburg specialist this morning and we will only hear the results tomorrow."

Coetzee said wing James Small was still battling with a hamstring strain, both hooker Naka Drotske and fly-half Henry Honiball were suffering with neck spasms and utility forward Fritz van Heerden had a bruised hip.

The South African squad, which flew to Durban from Cape Town on Monday to prepare for the second test, has been trimmed from 27 to 22 players but one or two additions were expected to be named within the next 24 hours, Coetzee said.
Provisional South African squad for the second test:

Andre Joubert, James Small, Japie Mulder, Andre Snyman, Henry Honiball, Joost van der Westhuizen, Gary Teichmann (captain), Andre Venter, Ruben Kruger, Fritz van Heerden, Hannes Strydom, Adrian Garvey, Naka Drotske, Os u Randt, Russell Bennett, Boeta Wessels, Werner Swanepoel, Mark Andrews, James Dalton, Dawie Theron, Fritz van Heerden, Percy Montgomery.
